1939, Second Team, ENGLAND
E. STIMPSON (-) next to official, with A.W. Penny (18) on his right. J.T. Holden (1st) is 6th from left.

PHOTOS:(R.Linstead)---Brian Buxton hands over to Chris Steer in the Walton Relay (top). Peter Whewell (A23) sets off for a fast lap in the Belgrave Relay while Buxton (A4) is seen finishing second on the first stage. No.64 is Our President who, by running in the Yacht handicap during his year of office, probably made history.

FRONT COVER (The Times) A photo to bring back memories. The great SYDNEY WOODERSON, former world record holder for the mile, runs alongside Belgrave's Past-President and former international, TED STIMPSON during Blackheath Harriers' Centenary 100X1 mile relay at Croydon Arena. For full details of the occasion see page 13.
Charlie Smart leads the 3 miles field in the Southern Counties A.A.A. Championships of 1939 at Motspur Park. Tom Carter (No. 32) lies 4th with Ted Stimpson (No. 25) 9th.

The Walking Section congratulate Joe Coleman following his election to the President's office. L to R; Back row. Carl Lawton, Mike Scamell, John Keown John Newman, Russell Day, John Dunsford. Middle. John Morris, Fred Denny, Richard Dorman, JOE COLEMAN, John Llewellin,Ed. Crossingham, Tom Carter, Ted Stimpson, Kneeling; Graham Seatter, Ron Day, John Hall.

Vern Blowfield hands the baton over to Ted who sets off on the second leg of the "News of the World" London to Brighton Relay held on April 19th 1947. The Bels went on to win by over two minutes.
(Editor's note: Actually we have stuck our necks out here, for the same combination of runners were also involved in the first take-over in April 1950, with Ted "running a blinder". No doubt someone will correct us if necessary).
